topic: What 5 ATM on a watch really means

lines.text: Your watch says five ATM... so why shouldn't it go in a hot shower?
Water pushes harder the deeper you go. Every ten metres adds one more atmosphere. Squeeze. Squeeze. Squeeze.
Watches fight back with seals. Rubber rings press into every gap... the crown, the buttons, the back.
Five ATM means a test at fifty metres of still water, for ten minutes. That's Samsung's own test.
But real life moves. A dive, a water jet, a hard stroke... they all spike the pressure past the test.
And heat is the sneaky part. Hot water and steam can weaken the seals, and seals wear out with age.
Pool, yes. Sauna, no. That's five ATM.

post.title: What 5 ATM on your watch really means
post.caption:
5 ATM on your watch doesn't mean "safe in any water" ⌚💧

5 ATM is a pressure rating: Samsung tests its 5ATM watches in 50 metres of still fresh water for 10 minutes. Every 10 metres of water adds about one atmosphere of pressure, and real life moves: a dive, a water jet or a hard stroke can push the pressure past that still-water test. Apple rates its watches WR50 under ISO 22810 for shallow-water activities like swimming in a pool or the sea, not scuba diving or high-velocity water.
Heat is the sneaky part: Samsung warns a sauna can damage water resistance, and the seals don't last forever.

Pool and sea swims: yes. Sauna, hot showers, diving: no. Send this to the friend who showers with their watch on.

Sources: Samsung Support (Galaxy Watch water resistance), Apple Developer (WR50, ISO 22810:2010), NOAA Ocean Service (water pressure).
keywords: can i shower with my smartwatch
can i swim with my watch

sources.note: Samsung Support, What is 5ATM? / Galaxy Watch water resistance: 5ATM tested by submerging the device in 50 metres of still fresh water for 10 minutes; the water-resistant feature can be damaged in a sauna; avoid pressure washers (a rapid increase in water pressure can exceed it); water resistance is not permanent (read 15 Nov 2026).

Apple Developer, WR50: water resistance rating of 50 metres under ISO 22810:2010; shallow-water activities like swimming in a pool or ocean; not scuba diving, waterskiing or other high-velocity water (read 15 Nov 2026).
NOAA Ocean Service, How does pressure change with ocean depth?: every 33 feet (10.06 metres) of seawater increases the pressure by one atmosphere (read 15 Nov 2026).
